html:
A violent earthquake that hit Constantinople on the night of 14 December 557, after smaller shocks earlier in the year. Writers of the time, among them the historian Agathias, say it nearly flattened the city.

It cracked the dome of Hagia Sophia, designed by Anthemius of Tralles and Isidore of Miletus. In May 558, while repairs were going on, the eastern part of the dome fell in. Isidore the Younger, nephew of the first architect, rebuilt it about 6 m higher and steeper, which made it more stable. The church was dedicated again in 562, and that dome still stands.

The quake also damaged the land walls. In 559 Kutrigur raiders came close to the capital before the aged Belisarius drove them off at the Battle of Melantias.
